# README summary
## Federal Register Monitor

A Federal Register monitoring Actor that queries the official federalregister.gov API to produce a structured, keyword-rich feed of daily US government publications (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents). It converts official Federal Register records into metadata records that include identifiers, titles, document types, publishing and effective dates, public comment deadlines and remaining days until close, agency associations, docket identifiers, links to Regulations.gov with live comment counts, abstracts, significance flags (EO‑12866), CFR references, and HTML/PDF URLs. Core capabilities include multi-mode retrieval (newest feed, imminent comment-deadline scanning, per-agency streams, keyword search across titles/abstracts, and documents tied to Regulations.gov dockets), client-side filtering by date/agency/type/significance, and continuous monitoring to build watchlists for regulatory action—all sourced from public API endpoints without a browser.

## Use cases

- Build a watchlist of proposed rules with public comment windows closing within a specified timeframe to prioritize regulatory responses.
- Monitor all publications from a single federal agency and generate daily or periodic digests of new actions.
- Run keyword monitoring across titles and abstracts to surface documents mentioning specific topics (e.g., artificial intelligence, airworthiness).
- Track documents linked to Regulations.gov dockets and surface live comment counts for stakeholder engagement.
- Consume a filtered daily feed of new Federal Register items by document type, agency, date range, or regulatory significance.
- Support regulatory affairs teams, trade associations, law firms, government contractors, and journalists with timely alerts on rulemakings and notices.

# README summary
## Regulations.gov Rulemaking Dockets Scraper

A Regulations.gov-focused data exporter that queries the official Regulations.gov v4 API to locate and extract structured regulatory records: dockets, documents, public comments, comment-period metadata, and attachment links with stable government identifiers and official source URLs. The Actor supports four workflows (dockets, documents, comments, and complete docket bundles), applies agency, document-type, posting-date, and comment-deadline filters, and can perform optional detail enrichment to retrieve abstracts, full comment text, public submitter fields, and file metadata (download URLs, formats, sizes). Technical features include paginated API requests with deduplication by official ID, configurable record limits per run, bounded retry/backoff for network and rate errors, and an automatic residential-proxy fallback after direct rate-limit responses; bundle exports preserve ordering (docket → documents → comments) and each saved observation includes official provenance and an extraction timestamp.

## Use cases

- Recurring regulatory monitoring for agency proposals, deadlines, and changes  
- Policy research and building repeatable longitudinal datasets across agencies  
- Compliance review and legal teams collecting records with official provenance  
- Government affairs teams tracking dockets that affect clients or industries  
- One-time docket export for audits or investigations  
- Journalists and civil-society analysts reviewing public participation in rulemaking  
- Data engineering: ingesting federal regulatory records and attachment metadata into warehouses or search indexes

# README summary
## Federal Register Search - Rules, Regulations, Notices & Executive Orders

Search and extract structured Federal Register records from the federalregister.gov API for rules, proposed rules, notices, and presidential documents. Supports keyword and agency/topic filtering, date-range and CFR title/part filtering, and publisher-significance filtering; tracks reported comment deadlines, publication and effective dates, docket/RIN/CFR references, issuing agencies, and regulatory-change indicators. Produces source-linked metadata and provenance evidence including official document links, exact API query provenance, retrieval timestamp, bounded-search context and ranking, and coverage/interpretation notes useful for regulatory monitoring, research, and downstream analysis.

## Use cases

- Regulatory compliance monitoring: track new and upcoming rules and proposed rules affecting specific industries or CFR parts.  
- Legal and policy research: search historical rulemaking activity by agency, topic, or CFR reference and retrieve abstracts and effective dates.  
- Government affairs and lobbying: find proposed rules with open comment periods to identify opportunities for public comments.  
- ESG and sustainability analysis: monitor agency rulemaking on climate, emissions, disclosure, and environment-related regulatory activity.  
- Investment and risk research: track economically significant rules that affect regulated sectors (healthcare, finance, energy, telecommunications).  
- Academic and think tank research: aggregate rulemaking data by agency, year, or significance for regulatory volume and trend analysis.

# README summary
## Federal Register Search - Rules, Regulations, Notices & Executive Orders

Search and extract structured Federal Register records from the federalregister.gov API for rules, proposed rules, notices, and presidential documents. Supports keyword and agency/topic filtering, date-range and CFR title/part filtering, and publisher-significance filtering; tracks reported comment deadlines, publication and effective dates, docket/RIN/CFR references, issuing agencies, and regulatory-change indicators. Produces source-linked metadata and provenance evidence including official document links, exact API query provenance, retrieval timestamp, bounded-search context and ranking, and coverage/interpretation notes useful for regulatory monitoring, research, and downstream analysis.

## Use cases

- Regulatory compliance monitoring: track new and upcoming rules and proposed rules affecting specific industries or CFR parts.  
- Legal and policy research: search historical rulemaking activity by agency, topic, or CFR reference and retrieve abstracts and effective dates.  
- Government affairs and lobbying: find proposed rules with open comment periods to identify opportunities for public comments.  
- ESG and sustainability analysis: monitor agency rulemaking on climate, emissions, disclosure, and environment-related regulatory activity.  
- Investment and risk research: track economically significant rules that affect regulated sectors (healthcare, finance, energy, telecommunications).  
- Academic and think tank research: aggregate rulemaking data by agency, year, or significance for regulatory volume and trend analysis.

# README summary
## Federal Register Search - Rules, Regulations, Notices & Executive Orders

Search and extract structured Federal Register records from the federalregister.gov API for rules, proposed rules, notices, and presidential documents. Supports keyword and agency/topic filtering, date-range and CFR title/part filtering, and publisher-significance filtering; tracks reported comment deadlines, publication and effective dates, docket/RIN/CFR references, issuing agencies, and regulatory-change indicators. Produces source-linked metadata and provenance evidence including official document links, exact API query provenance, retrieval timestamp, bounded-search context and ranking, and coverage/interpretation notes useful for regulatory monitoring, research, and downstream analysis.

## Use cases

- Regulatory compliance monitoring: track new and upcoming rules and proposed rules affecting specific industries or CFR parts.  
- Legal and policy research: search historical rulemaking activity by agency, topic, or CFR reference and retrieve abstracts and effective dates.  
- Government affairs and lobbying: find proposed rules with open comment periods to identify opportunities for public comments.  
- ESG and sustainability analysis: monitor agency rulemaking on climate, emissions, disclosure, and environment-related regulatory activity.  
- Investment and risk research: track economically significant rules that affect regulated sectors (healthcare, finance, energy, telecommunications).  
- Academic and think tank research: aggregate rulemaking data by agency, year, or significance for regulatory volume and trend analysis.

## Federal Register Scraper

A Federal Register search and metadata extraction Actor that locates and filters official U.S. Federal Register content—published rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents, and public inspection documents—and can also enumerate agencies. It performs keyword queries and structured filtering by agency, document category, date range, CFR title/part references, significance, and result ordering, with support for recurring monitoring and result limits. The Actor returns structured document metadata and official source links (HTML and PDF), including titles and summaries, publication and effective dates, comment deadlines, agency associations, docket and regulation identifiers, Federal Register citations, CFR references, page ranges, document numbers, and filing/typing information for public inspection entries.

## Use cases

- Compliance teams searching for rules and regulations relevant to specific policies or programs (for example, H‑1B notices).
- Policy researchers and lawyers collecting published documents and proposed rules by topic, agency, or date.
- Journalists finding notices, proposed rules, and presidential documents with official links and citations.
- Tracking proposed rules or rulemaking activity by topic, agency, or time window.
- Collecting agency listings and agency metadata from the Federal Register.
- Monitoring new Federal Register documents over time to capture documents not previously seen by a prior search.

# README summary
## Federal Register Search

Searches the U.S. Federal Register via the Government Publishing Office (GPO) API to locate and return structured, machine-readable regulatory records (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents including executive orders) for keyword-driven and filtered queries. The Actor performs full-text keyword matching across titles, abstracts, and document text, applies agency, document-type, date-range, and economic-significance filters, paginates and rate-limits API requests, and transforms nested Federal Register responses into flat, analysis-ready JSON records containing regulatory metadata: primary and all agency names, human-readable CFR references, extracted regulation identifier numbers (RINs), Federal Register citations and signing/publication/effective dates, abstracts, significance flags for Executive Order 12866, and direct HTML/PDF links to official documents; covers the Federal Register archive back to 1994.

## Use cases

- Regulatory compliance monitoring to track new final rules and proposed rules from agencies relevant to a business or sector.  
- Policy research and trend analysis across the Federal Register archive by keyword, agency, and date range.  
- Legal research to locate rules, notices, and presidential documents with structured citation data and CFR references.  
- Lobbying and government affairs monitoring to catch proposed rules during public comment periods.  
- Journalism and investigative reporting focused on executive orders, significant rules, and agency actions.  
- Academic research building structured datasets of regulatory actions for political science, economics, and public policy studies.  
- Building compliance dashboards that track regulatory obligations with CFR references, effective dates, and RIN identifiers.  
- Executive order tracking and aggregation of presidential documents (executive orders, proclamations, memoranda).  
- Multi-agency rulemaking analysis to identify and analyze joint rulemakings involving multiple agencies.  
- Surveillance of economically significant rules by filtering for regulations designated under Executive Order 12866.

# README summary
## Federal Register Intelligence

A data-extraction Actor that harvests US Federal Register content—regulations, rules, notices, proposed regulations and official government actions—and returns clean, validated structured JSON records (22 fields per record). It indexes and normalizes regulatory metadata and document content for tracking regulatory change, compliance monitoring, legal research, media updates, and alerting. Technical capabilities include multi-mode collection (recent publications, keyword search, public-inspection listings, and agency-focused retrieval), filtering by document type/agency/date ranges and result limits, live fetches from the Federal Register, continuous maintenance of parsing logic, and output that includes document identifiers and titles, publication and effective dates, document types, agency metadata, docket/regulation identifiers, regulatory citations, comment/deadline information, and links to full-text HTML/PDFs.

## Use cases

- Compliance / risk — monitor regulations, recalls, and filings  
- News / media — auto-update on official government actions  
- Legal-tech — track rules affecting clients  
- Research / policy — analyze government data at scale  
- Alerting — notify stakeholders of relevant changes

## Federal Register Search - Rules, Regulations, Notices & Executive Orders

Search and extract structured Federal Register records from the federalregister.gov API for rules, proposed rules, notices, and presidential documents. Supports keyword and agency/topic filtering, date-range and CFR title/part filtering, and publisher-significance filtering; tracks reported comment deadlines, publication and effective dates, docket/RIN/CFR references, issuing agencies, and regulatory-change indicators. Produces source-linked metadata and provenance evidence including official document links, exact API query provenance, retrieval timestamp, bounded-search context and ranking, and coverage/interpretation notes useful for regulatory monitoring, research, and downstream analysis.

## Use cases

- Regulatory compliance monitoring: track new and upcoming rules and proposed rules affecting specific industries or CFR parts.  
- Legal and policy research: search historical rulemaking activity by agency, topic, or CFR reference and retrieve abstracts and effective dates.  
- Government affairs and lobbying: find proposed rules with open comment periods to identify opportunities for public comments.  
- ESG and sustainability analysis: monitor agency rulemaking on climate, emissions, disclosure, and environment-related regulatory activity.  
- Investment and risk research: track economically significant rules that affect regulated sectors (healthcare, finance, energy, telecommunications).  
- Academic and think tank research: aggregate rulemaking data by agency, year, or significance for regulatory volume and trend analysis.

finalAnswer:
**Yes, the rule is in effect, but several of its compliance deadlines have been pushed back.** The rule itself was never stayed or vacated, as far as I could find.

**What the document is**
- It is EPA's "Oil and Natural Gas Sector Climate Review" final rule, 89 FR 16820 (document 2024-00366), published March 8, 2024. It created the methane and VOC standards known as OOOOb for new sources and OOOOc for existing sources.
- The Federal Register page lists the **effective date as May 7, 2024**.

**Delays and changes I found**
1. **August 2024 correction.** The Federal Register page flags a newer related document (2024-13206), an "Interim final rule; correction; request for comments" published 08/01/2024. I did not open it.
2. **July 31, 2025 interim final rule.** EPA extended several compliance deadlines. According to EPA's FAQ page:
   - Deadlines for control devices, equipment leaks, storage vessels, process controllers, and covers/closed vent systems moved to 18 months after the interim rule was published.
   - That includes the continuous-pilot-flame and alarm requirements for flares and enclosed combustion devices.
   - A trade-press summary (All4Inc) says the state plan deadline moved to January 22, 2027.
3. **Final action on that interim rule, announced November 26, 2025.** It was published December 3, 2025 as 2025-21788, "Extension of Deadlines in Standards of Performance…". EPA says it saves about $750 million in compliance costs over 11 years. A search snippet says the "no identifiable emissions" inspection requirements were extended to January 22, 2027.

**Caveats**
- The extensions apply to specific compliance dates. They did not delay the rule's May 7, 2024 effective date.
- I did not read the full text of the December 2025 rule. Check it for the exact extended dates for each requirement.
- I did not check court challenges or anything after December 2025, such as further reconsideration or rescission proceedings. For current status, look at the "newer documents" links on the Federal Register page and at EPA's oil and gas rule page.

Sources:
- https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/03/08/2024-00366/standards-of-performance-for-new-reconstructed-and-modified-sources-and-emissions-guidelines-for-existing
- https://www.epa.gov/controlling-air-pollution-oil-and-natural-gas-operations/2025-interim-final-rule-extend-compliance
- https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/12/03/2025-21788/oil-and-natural-gas-sector-climate-review-extension-of-deadlines-in-standards-of-performance-for-new

## Frequently Asked Questions

**How does the July 2025 interim final rule impact my compliance requirements?**

The July 2025 interim final rule extended several compliance deadlines from the [2024 final rule](https://gcc02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.epa.gov%2Fcontrolling-air-pollution-oil-and-natural-gas-industry%2Fepas-final-rule-oil-and-natural-gas&data=05%7C02%7CBailey.Jarod%40epa.gov%7C05d68147f99d48db6a3008ddd3912d99%7C88b378b367484867acf976aacbeca6a7%7C0%7C0%7C638899342663601635%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=sJvd51eCygNRL%2FqYWbTva4SJDUoX0sgnw6C64i9D4xk%3D&reserved=0). The reporting deadlines associated with these compliance deadlines were also extended as a practical matter. We note that in this interim final rule, we are extending compliance deadlines in the 2024 NSPS as follows:

*   The deadline to meet certain requirements related to control devices, equipment leaks, storage vessels, process controllers, and covers/closed vent systems will be extended to 18 months after the interim final rule is published in the Federal Register. 
    *   This includes extending the deadline to require that flares and enclosed combustion devices used to control emissions have a continuous pilot flame and for an alarm to be sent to the nearest control room if the pilot or combustion flame is not lit. 

**When does the comment period for the interim final rule close?**

The July 2025 interim final rule comment period closes on September 2, 2025. EPA encourages readers to submit comments on the interim final rule during the comment period, particularly related to the above FAQ. To submit comments on the July 2025 interim final rule, see [Docket ID No. EPA–HQ– OAR–2025–0162.](https://www.regulations.gov/docket/EPA-HQ-OAR-2025-0162)

## November 2025 Final Interim Final Rule

November 26, 2025 -- EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin is taking final action on the agency’s July 2025 Interim Final Rule (IFR) to extend several compliance deadlines in the Biden-Harris Administration’s Clean Air Act (CAA) rules for the oil and gas industry – commonly known as OOOOb/c. By providing more realistic timelines for owners and operators of new and modified oil and natural gas sources, the Trump EPA is taking an important step in unleashing America’s domestic energy supply. The action will impact hundreds of thousands of oil and gas sources across the country and save an estimated $750 million over 11 years in compliance costs. 

*   [2025 Final Interim Final Rule](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/12/03/2025-21788/oil-and-natural-gas-sector-climate-review-extension-of-deadlines-in-standards-of-performance-for-new)
*   [EPA's Final Oil and Natural Gas Interim Final Rule Fact Sheet (pdf)](https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2025-11/fact-sheet_o-g_final-ifr_20251124.pdf) (161.22 KB)

## July 2025 Interim Final Rule

July 28, 2025 -- EPA took an important step in unleashing the Nation’s domestic energy supply by extending several compliance deadlines in the Biden-Harris Administration’s Clean Air Act rules for the oil and natural gas industry - commonly known as OOOOb/c. In an interim final rule, EPA is providing more realistic timelines for owners and operators of new and modified oil and natural gas sources across the country. In addition, the agency is giving states additional time to submit plans under the 2024 Emissions Guidelines to limit methane emissions from hundreds of thousands of existing oil and natural gas sources across the country.

finalAnswer:
Yes. The Department of Labor proposal with RIN 1235-AA52 was withdrawn. The Federal Register record shows the withdrawal was published on 2026-10-07.

- **Title:** "Statements of General Policy or Interpretation Not Directly Related to Regulations". The Wage and Hour Division issued it.
- **Proposed rule:** Published 2025-07-02 (FR Doc. 2025-12314), with comments closing 2025-08-01. The comment period was not extended.
- **Withdrawal:** "Withdrawal of Proposed Rule" (FR Doc. 2026-20523), published 2026-10-07. It is the latest official action on this RIN.
- **Final rule:** None was ever published.
- **Docket:** WHD-2025-0002 on Regulations.gov.

Sources: [Proposed rule](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/07/02/2025-12314/statements-of-general-policy-or-interpretation-not-directly-related-to-regulations) and [withdrawal notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/07/2026-20523/statements-of-general-policy-or-interpretation-not-directly-related-to-regulations-withdrawal-of).

The match was by RIN, with high confidence. This covers the Federal Register and Regulations.gov record only, not court actions or enforcement policy.

# README summary
## GovInfo Scraper

GovInfo Scraper queries the U.S. Government Publishing Office (GovInfo) documented public API to retrieve structured metadata and direct document links for federal documents — including congressional bills, enacted public laws, the daily Congressional Record, committee hearings and reports, the Federal Register, and federal court opinions. For each document it emits a single structured record containing a stable package identifier and collection code, short title (popular title), optional official long title (from the package record), congress and bill metadata parsed from the package identifier (congress number, bill type and number, document version), publication and last-modified dates, issuing bodies, and direct public links to the PDF and full-text HTML. The Actor uses the documented api.govinfo.gov search route (API key supported), follows cursor-based pagination (offset cursor), reads rate-limit headers per response, retries transient server errors with linear backoff, logs per-collection results and failures, and supports optional per-document package-record fetches (extra API requests) to include official abstracts/long titles. It runs without a browser, proxies, or GovInfo account and is designed to support scheduled monitoring and downstream document ingestion pipelines.

## Use cases

- Legislative tracking for policy teams (watch bills and enacted laws; diff on package identifiers between runs)  
- Build a bill-monitoring alert product (keyword-scoped, newest-first monitoring)  
- Legal research corpora (collect federal court opinions, committee hearings, reports, with direct text links for ingest)  
- Scheduled monitoring / automated sweeps of selected GovInfo collections and date ranges  
- Feeding document ingestion pipelines with direct PDF and full-text HTML links and structured metadata

finalAnswer:
**Short answer: I found no sign that a federal court has blocked the current EPA methane rule.** The sources I could read don't show that any court has stayed, vacated or paused it. My search was limited, so I can't rule out a very recent order.

**What the sources show:**
- **2024 rule:** The D.C. Circuit refused to stay the rule on July 9, 2024. The Supreme Court also denied a stay on Oct. 4, 2024 (*Oklahoma v. EPA*, No. 24A213), with no recorded dissents. The merits case, *Texas v. EPA* (No. 24-1054), was later put on hold in February 2025 while the Trump EPA reconsidered the rule.
- **Rollbacks by the EPA itself:** Harvard's Environmental & Energy Law Program tracker (last updated June 8, 2026) says EPA extended compliance deadlines in 2025. It then issued a final rule on April 6, 2026 that loosens requirements for flares and vent gas.
- **Current litigation:** Environmental groups are challenging the EPA's rollbacks, not defending a court block. EDF filed a petition on June 8, 2026 against the April rule (No. 26-1152, D.C. Cir.). Other environmental groups sued in 2025 over the deadline extensions.
- **Related measures:** Congress used the Congressional Review Act to repeal the methane Waste Emissions Charge rule. The charge itself remains in the statute, and Congress barred EPA from collecting it until 2034.

**Older headlines:** Search results included "Court Blocks E.P.A. Effort to Suspend Obama-Era Methane…" and "Federal Appeals Court Issues Temporary Stay of EPA Rule…". I couldn't open those pages. The first appears to be the 2017 D.C. Circuit decision that vacated EPA's delay of the Obama-era rule. I don't know which rule the second one refers to. I also couldn't read the "Federal court blocks Trump EPA on air pollution" result, so I can't say what it covers.

If you mean a specific recent ruling, tell me the rule or the date. I can look for it directly. For a definitive answer, check the D.C. Circuit docket for No. 26-1152 or the Harvard EELP tracker.

# Supreme Court declines to block EPA methane, mercury rules

![amy-howe thumbnail](/_next/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fpito4za5%2Fproduction%2F05a8a23fd24f6e9a1c433f8483a0820aeda4a2fa-600x601.webp%3Fw%3D2000%26h%3D2000%26fit%3Dcrop%26crop%3Dfocalpoint&w=96&q=75)

By[Amy Howe](https://www.scotusblog.com/author/amy-howe/)

/Oct 4, 2024

![The,United,States,Supreme,Court,Is,Seen,In,Washington,,Dc,](/_next/image/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fcdn.sanity.io%2Fimages%2Fpito4za5%2Fproduction%2F5f7be476092efa7b9f75a9dc70ffab7c0e2e4324-2560x1707.jpg%3Fw%3D2000&w=1920&q=75)

(MattCC716 via Flickr)

The Supreme Court on Friday turned down a request from Republican-led states and industry groups to block a rule from the Environmental Protection Agency that imposes more stringent standards on emissions of hazardous air pollutants from coal-fired power plants. At the same time, the justices turned down a similar request from Oklahoma and industry groups to block an EPA rule that seeks to regulate emissions of methane, a powerful greenhouse gas, from crude-oil and natural gas facilities.

Friday’s orders mean that both rules will remain in effect while challenges to them move forward in a federal appeals court in Washington, D.C.

The orders leaving the EPA rules in place come three months after the Supreme Court put another EPA rule, intended to reduce air pollution that affects air quality in “downwind” states, on hold while challenges to it continue in the lower courts.

The EPA issued the first rule as part of the “Hazardous Air Pollutants” program established by the Clean Air Act, which targets pollutants – such as mercury, arsenic, and nickel – that can be toxic for humans.

The challengers – which include 23 Republican-led states, power plants, mining companies, and industry groups – went to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit seeking review of the rule. They also asked the court of appeals to put the rule on hold while the litigation went forward, but the D.C. Circuit rejected that request. The challengers then came to the Supreme Court in August, filing seven separate applications to stay the rule while the D.C. Circuit’s review continued.

The challengers complained that the new rule will impose billions of dollars in costs on power plants without providing any real public health benefits. Instead, the challengers suggested, the rule is part of a broader plan to (as the states, led by North Dakota contended) “force a nationwide transition away from coal for putative climate change reasons – pursuing a national policy choice this Court has expressly held the agency lacks authority to make.”

The EPA published the methane rule in March. Here too Oklahoma and the industry groups went first to the D.C. Circuit, seeking to challenge the rule and to have that court put it on hold while the litigation continued. The D.C. Circuit denied the request for a stay in July, prompting the challengers to come to the Supreme Court in August.

In brief unsigned orders on Friday, the justices turned down both sets of requests to put the rules on hold. The justices did not provide any explanation for their decisions, and there were no recorded dissents.

The court has not yet acted on a third set of requests to stay a different EPA rule, aimed at reducing emissions of carbon dioxide by power plants. Those requests were filed beginning in late July and have been fully briefed for over a month.

_This article was [originally published at Howe on the Court](https://amylhowe.com/2024/10/04/supreme-court-declines-to-block-epa-methane-mercury-rules/)._

# EPA VOC and Methane Standards for Oil and Gas Facilities

Last updated:

June 8, 2026

Agencies

[EPA](https://eelp.law.harvard.edu/agency/epa/)

Actions

Slated for Rollback

![Pipes with valves on water with sun setting int he distance over trees.](https://eelp.law.harvard.edu/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/iStock-1468710968.jpg)

[Current Status](https://eelp.law.harvard.edu/tracker/epa-voc-and-methane-standards-for-oil-and-gas-facilities-2/#status) [Why it Matters](https://eelp.law.harvard.edu/tracker/epa-voc-and-methane-standards-for-oil-and-gas-facilities-2/#why-it-matters) [Key Resources](https://eelp.law.harvard.edu/tracker/epa-voc-and-methane-standards-for-oil-and-gas-facilities-2/#key-resources) [Timeline](https://eelp.law.harvard.edu/tracker/epa-voc-and-methane-standards-for-oil-and-gas-facilities-2/#timeline) [Experts](https://eelp.law.harvard.edu/tracker/epa-voc-and-methane-standards-for-oil-and-gas-facilities-2/#experts)

## Current Status

In 2024, EPA finalized [three rules](https://eelp.law.harvard.edu/methane-rules-for-the-oil-and-gas-sector/) regulating methane from the oil and gas sector: [regulations](https://eelp.law.harvard.edu/epas-final-methane-rule-incorporating-advanced-technologies-and-emissions-data-to-reduce-methane-emissions-from-the-oil-and-natural-gas-sector/) for VOCs and methane from the oil and gas sector (NSPS OOOOb/EG OOOOc), [revisions to the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program Subpart W](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2024-05-14/pdf/2024-08988.pdf), and implementation of the [Waste Emissions Charge](https://eelp.law.harvard.edu/final-rule-implementing-the-waste-emissions-charge-for-petroleum-and-natural-gas-systems/) in the Inflation Reduction Act, which has been repealed by the Congressional Review Act. In March 2025, Congress prohibited EPA from collecting the Waste Emissions Charge until 2034. In September, EPA proposed to delay the [Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program Subpart W program](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2025-09-16/pdf/2025-17923.pdf) until 2034. In November 2025, [EPA finalized the deadline exemptions](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/12/03/2025-21788/oil-and-natural-gas-sector-climate-review-extension-of-deadlines-in-standards-of-performance-for-new) for certain provisions of the NSPS OOOOb/ EG OOOOc rule.

## Why it Matters

Methane is a powerful greenhouse gas released from oil and gas production, processing, transmission, and storage through equipment leaks, venting, and flaring. As technologies advance to better detect and reduce methane emissions and markets develop to demand gas with lower methane emissions, there is an opportunity to design state and federal regulations that align such incentives and ensure methane emission reductions

During the Obama administration, EPA set standards for volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and methane emissions for new oil and natural gas sources (which included production, processing, transmission, and storage). This was the first rule expressly targeting methane emissions. The first Trump administration revoked nearly all of these standards, leaving in place only some of the standards controlling VOCs from new sources. See EELP’s analysis of the first Trump rescissions, [EPA’s Final Methane Emissions Rules Roll Back Standards and Statutory Authority](https://eelp.law.harvard.edu/epas-final-methane-emissions-rule-rolls-back-standards-and-statutory-authority/).

Starting in 2021, the Biden administration and Congress took steps to reinstate and expand the Obama-era methane standards for new and existing oil and natural gas sources. On June 30, 2021, President Biden signed a Congressional Review Act resolution [passed](https://www.congress.gov/bill/117th-congress/senate-joint-resolution/14/actions) by Congress that revoked the Trump administration’s rule. The US also jointly announced a [methane reduction pledge](https://www.globalmethanepledge.org/) with the EU in September 2021, ahead of COP26. Now over 155 countries are participating, with each agreeing to undertake voluntary actions to collectively contribute to reducing global methane emissions by 30 percent from 2020 levels by 2030.

The second Trump administration is taking initial regulatory actions to pause the collection of methane emissions from the oil and natural gas sector, eliminate the legal foundation for regulating greenhouse gas emissions under the Clean Air Act, and reconsider the regulations requiring methane emission reductions.

prompt: What did the Supreme Court decide in Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo?
finalAnswer:
I didn't run any Actors. Court-opinion scrapers exist in the Store, but this is a settled, well-documented decision, so I answered from what I know.

**Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo (June 28, 2024)**

The Supreme Court ruled 6–3 that courts must use their own independent judgment to decide what a statute means. They may not defer to a federal agency's reasonable interpretation of an ambiguous statute. This overruled ***Chevron U.S.A. v. NRDC* (1984)**, which had required that deference. Chief Justice Roberts wrote the majority opinion. Justices Sotomayor, Kagan and Jackson dissented. Justice Jackson did not take part in the companion case from the First Circuit, *Relentless, Inc. v. Department of Commerce*, which was decided together with this one.

**Background:** Herring fishing companies challenged a National Marine Fisheries Service rule. The rule required fishing vessels to pay for the onboard observers who monitor compliance. The agency based this on the Magnuson-Stevens Act. The lower courts upheld the rule under *Chevron* deference.

**Reasoning:**
- **Administrative Procedure Act:** Section 706 directs courts to "decide all relevant questions of law" and interpret statutory provisions. The Court said this makes statutory interpretation a judicial job, not an agency's.
- **Chevron's premise:** The Court rejected the idea that statutory ambiguity means Congress delegated gap-filling power to the agency. It called that presumption a fiction.
- **Delegation still counts:** When Congress explicitly gives an agency discretion, such as by using terms like "appropriate" or "reasonable", courts must respect it. Their job is to police the limits of that delegation.
- **Respect for agency views:** Agency interpretations can still carry persuasive weight under *Skidmore v. Swift & Co.* (1944), based on their thoroughness and consistency. They no longer get binding deference.
- **Precedent:** The Court said earlier cases decided under *Chevron* keep their force under stare decisis. The fact that *Chevron* was later overruled is not by itself a reason to reopen them.

**Significance:** The decision shifts interpretive power from agencies to courts and makes it easier to challenge federal regulations. The dissent argued that agencies have the relevant expertise and that the ruling gives judges policy decisions they are less suited to make.

prompt: When does California's SB 253 climate disclosure law take effect?
finalAnswer:
I didn't run an Actor. This is a legal-timeline question I can answer from what I know, but my information may be out of date.

**SB 253 (the Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act)** applies to U.S. companies that do business in California and have more than $1 billion in annual revenue. Its phases are:

- **Scope 1 and 2 emissions (direct and purchased-energy emissions):** The first reports are due in **2026**, covering fiscal year 2025 data. Under SB 219, which amended the law in 2024, the California Air Resources Board (CARB) sets the exact deadline. CARB's proposed first deadline was **August 10, 2026**.
- **Scope 3 emissions (value-chain emissions):** The first reports are due in **2027**, covering fiscal year 2026 data. CARB is still setting the details.
- **Assurance:** Scope 1 and 2 data need limited assurance starting in 2026. That rises to reasonable assurance in 2030. Scope 3 data need limited assurance starting in 2030.

**SB 261**, the companion climate-risk report law, is a separate statute. Its January 1, 2026 start was put on hold by a court injunction in late 2025. SB 253 was not affected.

The CARB regulations and deadlines were still being finalized and litigated when I last had information. Check CARB's website for the current deadlines before you rely on these dates. I can run a web search to look for the latest status if you'd like.

# README summary
## SEC EDGAR Scraper

A data-extraction Actor that ingests U.S. SEC EDGAR data via the SEC’s official APIs (data.sec.gov, efts.sec.gov, www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar) and emits structured, normalized records for regulatory filings and financial data. Core capabilities include harvesting filing metadata (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, amendments, etc.), extracting raw XBRL facts and normalized financial statements (income, balance sheet, cash flow) mapped to US-GAAP concepts, surfacing full-text search hits across filings, parsing insider transaction reports, exporting institutional (13F) holdings, detecting activist filings (SC 13D/G), and parsing itemized 8-K content. The Actor resolves company identifiers to canonical SEC CIKs, adheres to SEC fair-use rate limits, can produce optional AI-generated filing summaries, and is implemented in TypeScript on the Apify SDK.

## Use cases

- Financial analysts: obtain normalized income statements, balance sheets, and cash flows for U.S. public companies without manual XBRL parsing.  
- Hedge funds & quantitative teams: monitor insider trades, institutional 13F holdings, and activist filings as they are filed.  
- M&A and private equity deal teams: auto-parse 8-K item codes to surface acquisition, executive-change, and auditor-change signals in near real-time.  
- Investment research and AI/LLM teams: ingest multi-year filing archives with structured metadata and optional AI summaries for model training and analysis.  
- Compliance and governance teams: track proxy statements, disclosure trends, and peer filings within date ranges and incremental update runs.  
- Document search and surveillance: full-text search across filings for keyword mentions and regulatory language monitoring.

Supports keyword full-text search across comments, docket-level restriction, date filtering, an option to fetch full bodies (one extra API call per comment), and supplying an API key for higher request throughput; can run with zero configuration to return recent comments. ## Use cases - Government affairs & lobbying: monitor who and what organizations are arguing for or against proposed rules and capture their arguments. - Legal & compliance: read substantive objections to anticipate litigation angles and agency responses. - Policy research & journalism: quantify support vs. opposition, surface mass-comment campaigns, and extract quotable submissions. - Competitive intelligence: track when competitors file comments and what regulatory positions they take. - AI / LLM pipelines: ingest full comment text for summarization, stance detection, entity extraction, or other NLP workflows. # [Input schema](https://apify.com/bikram07/regulations-gov-comments/input) ```json {"title":"Regulations.gov Comments input","type":"object","schemaVersion":1,"properties":{"searchTerm":{"title":"Search term (optional)","description":"Full-text search across comments. # README summary
## Federal Register Search

Searches the U.S. Federal Register via the Government Publishing Office (GPO) API to locate and return structured, machine-readable regulatory records (rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents including executive orders) for keyword-driven and filtered queries. The Actor performs full-text keyword matching across titles, abstracts, and document text, applies agency, document-type, date-range, and economic-significance filters, paginates and rate-limits API requests, and transforms nested Federal Register responses into flat, analysis-ready JSON records containing regulatory metadata: primary and all agency names, human-readable CFR references, extracted regulation identifier numbers (RINs), Federal Register citations and signing/publication/effective dates, abstracts, significance flags for Executive Order 12866, and direct HTML/PDF links to official documents; covers the Federal Register archive back to 1994.

## Use cases

- Regulatory compliance monitoring to track new final rules and proposed rules from agencies relevant to a business or sector.  
- Policy research and trend analysis across the Federal Register archive by keyword, agency, and date range.  
- Legal research to locate rules, notices, and presidential documents with structured citation data and CFR references.  
- Lobbying and government affairs monitoring to catch proposed rules during public comment periods.  
- Journalism and investigative reporting focused on executive orders, significant rules, and agency actions.  
- Academic research building structured datasets of regulatory actions for political science, economics, and public policy studies.  
- Building compliance dashboards that track regulatory obligations with CFR references, effective dates, and RIN identifiers.  
- Executive order tracking and aggregation of presidential documents (executive orders, proclamations, memoranda).  
- Multi-agency rulemaking analysis to identify and analyze joint rulemakings involving multiple agencies.  
- Surveillance of economically significant rules by filtering for regulations designated under Executive Order 12866.

# README summary
## eCFR Scraper — US Code of Federal Regulations

Converts the eCFR's XML into clean, section-level JSON records for the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR): one record per CFR section with location metadata (title number and name, chapter, part, subpart, section identifier), heading and legal citation, cleaned full text and discrete paragraph units, and the full hierarchical ancestry from chapter to section. Uses the official eCFR versioner API to fetch snapshots by date and transforms nested regulatory XML into normalized, searchable JSON suitable for text analytics, NLP, full-text search, and downstream retrieval workflows. Supports targeted extraction by chapter/part/subpart and version-dated snapshots to reproduce the CFR as of specified dates, enabling structured outputs optimized for regulatory datasets, semantic search, and RAG pipelines.

## Use cases

- Create legal and compliance datasets from federal regulations at the section level.  
- Monitor regulatory changes and track CFR updates over time using dated snapshots.  
- Feed cleaned section-level texts and hierarchical metadata into RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) and other NLP pipelines.  
- Produce structured inputs for full-text search, indexing, and semantic search over federal regulations.  
- Convert nested eCFR XML into normalized JSON for downstream analysis, citation extraction, and hierarchy-aware processing.

**Result: 16 active USCG notices fall within 1 nm of your route (14.35 nm). The check was partial, so don't treat this as a complete clearance.**

The check ran at 2026-10-08 21:03 UTC with a 1 nm corridor on each side. Nothing was upcoming or expired. The one safety-zone dataset I couldn't check is described at the end.

**Notices that intersect the route itself**
- **Survey operations (Monmouth Univ./Equinor), through Nov 1.** The R/V OCEAN HAWK is recovering unmarked seafloor moorings in New York Harbor and along the export cable corridor. The notice says the moorings have no surface buoys and the vessel monitors VHF 16/13. It intersects near the southern leg, about 15% along the route.
- **Sailing regatta, Upper Bay south of Governors Island, through Oct 18.** It runs Wed/Thu 6–9 pm, Sat 12–5 pm, and Sun Oct 18 12–5 pm. It is about 35% along the route.
- **Three weekly sailing regattas, Upper Bay between Ellis and Governors Islands, 6:30–8:00 pm.** One runs Tuesdays through Oct 13, one Wednesdays through Oct 14, and one Thursdays through Oct 15. They are about 49% along the route and use VHF 68.
- **Manhattan circumnavigation swim events, through Oct 13.** Swimmers are escorted by safety vessels and kayaks. Oct 8–13 starts are mostly morning to mid-afternoon from Pier A (VHF 6). It is about 56% along the route.

**Notices near the route but not on it**
- **Sunken barge hazard, Anchorage 21-A.** It is 0.07 nm from the route and in effect through Mar 27, 2027. The barge is in about 13 ft of water and marked by 4 buoys with strobes.
- **Marine construction.** Several sites sit within 1 nm of your track:
  - Governors Island fender wharf rehab, 0.68 nm away, weekdays through Nov 30.
  - Liberty State Park barges, 0.54 nm away, through Oct 31.
  - Trevcon/Battery Park City work at Reaches 06 and 02 and the North Cove dredging, 0.003–0.03 nm away. These have barges moved by tug at any hour, run through 2027–2029, and monitor VHF 13/16/65–75.
  - Hudson Tunnel Project cofferdam and barges off Pier 66, 0.52 nm away, through Jan 2027.
  - Manhattan Cruise Terminal dredging, 0.58 nm away, through Oct 10, 24 hours a day, on VHF 78/13/16.
  - Pier 94 pile repairs, 0.52 nm away, through June 2027.
- **Safety zone, 33 CFR 165.T01-0336, Hudson River off Pier 66.** It is 0.52 nm from the route and enforced through Jan 20, 2029. Entry needs COTP New York permission on VHF 16 or (718) 354-4353. This zone is not on your track, but you would need that permission if you deviated into it.

**Limits of this check**
- **Safety-zone coverage is incomplete.** NAVCEN's `safeZoneLine_1` dataset returned a 404 and wasn't checked. Line-type safety zones could therefore be missing.
- **Out of scope:** Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices, aids-to-navigation discrepancies, NOAA/NGA warnings, AIS, weather and tides.
- **Not navigational advice.** Before you go, confirm with the current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners, VHF broadcasts and Captain of the Port New York.

finalAnswer:
Yes. The U.S. Coast Guard's navigation safety feed (NAVCEN) lists 14 notices within 1 nautical mile of a straight line between your two points. Most are dredging and construction work in the Houston Ship Channel and Galveston Bay. None is a formal closure, but several ask vessels to coordinate, slow down or avoid meeting near the work. The check ran on 2026-10-08.

**Caveat:** the Coast Guard's safety-zone layer, which holds formal closures and security zones, was not published and couldn't be checked. So I can't rule out a safety zone on this route. Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices and non-Coast Guard sources (NOAA, NGA, AIS, weather) were also not covered.

**Dredging and marine construction (in effect)**
- **Galveston Bay pipeline installation (until about 2027-03-01):**
  - It sits east of Houston Ship Channel Light 42, about a third of the way along your route.
  - Crews and vessels work 24 hours a day.
  - By about Nov 1, equipment will be within 1,800 ft of both sides of the channel.
  - Transit at your slowest safe speed.
- **Houston Ship Channel dredging between Lights 78 and 92 (Dredge R.B. Weeks, ends 2026-10-10):**
  - It runs 24/7.
  - Avoid meeting or overtaking near the dredges.
  - Contact them on VHF 13 or 16.
- **Barbours Cut dredging (Dredge DB Catalina, until further notice):**
  - It is within 0.03 nm of your route.
  - The dredge asks for 30 minutes' notice if you are going to or from Barbours Terminal Channel.
  - Contact them on VHF 13 or 81.
- **Morgans Point and Barbours Terminal dredging and bulkhead work (until 2027-07-01):**
  - It runs 24/7.
  - Watch for dive flags and day shapes.
  - Contact them on VHF 13 or 16.
- **Houston Ship Channel dredging, Lighted Buoy 95 to Light 109A (Dredge Nimitz, 2026-10-14 to 2026-12-31):**
  - It starts in about a week, near the end of your route.
  - Coordinate with the dredge at least 45 minutes ahead so it can move equipment out of the channel.
  - Contact them on VHF 13, 16 or 79.
- **Cedar Bayou Channel dredging and berm construction (until 2026-12-31):**
  - It is about 0.8 nm off the route.
  - It runs 24/7.

**Aids to navigation (temporary changes, no end dates)**
- Galveston Bay Entrance Channel Lighted Buoy 12 has a temporary change (about 0.8 nm off the route).
- The Lower Galveston Bay Inner Range front and rear lights have temporary changes.
- Houston Ship Channel Light 91 is discontinued for dredging.

**Advisories**
- **Houston VTS directive:** no barge work in the Houston Ship Channel between Morgans Point and Exxon to go into or out of the USI Canal.
- **Menhaden season:** schools of fish can clog sea strainers and cooling systems (Sector Houston-Galveston bulletin).
- **Hurricane season:** a general Coast Guard bulletin applies through Nov 30. It describes Port Conditions Whiskey, X-Ray, Yankee and Zulu, where Zulu means the port is closed.

The route is only the straight line between your two points. The tool doesn't plan a navigable path, and the line probably crosses land in places. Confirm with current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners, VHF broadcasts and VTS Houston-Galveston before you go. This is not navigational advice.

U.S. Coast Guard Heartland District Hurricane Season 2026 --- The 2026 Hurricane Season extends from June 1, 2026 through November 30, 2026.  Tropical storms and hurricanes often develop with little warning.  Extensive damage to small craft often results in loss of life.  All mariners, particularly operators of small fishing vessels, are reminded that advanced planning, which may prevent loss of vessel and crew, should include:  
a) Instruction of crew and passengers in location of emergency equipment and emergency procedures.
b) Pre-sailing check of vessel, machinery, and equipment for seaworthiness.
c) Installation of strong ground tackle.
d) Review of storm center evacuation procedures.
e) Knowledge of the nearest hurricane shelter or port of refuge.
f) Constant radio watch on VHF-FM Channel 16 and frequent monitoring of VHF-FM Weather Channel for National Weather Service Broadcasts.


• AIDS TO NAVIGATION/WRECKS/OBSTRUCTIONS: As a result of tropical storms and hurricanes, aids to navigation along the Gulf Coast and on structures in the Gulf of America and surrounding waters may become damaged or destroyed.  Buoys may move from assigned positions, be damaged, extinguished, sunk, or otherwise made inoperative.  Mariners should not solely rely upon the position or operation of an aid to navigation, but should employ such other available methods of determining positions.  Wrecks, submerged obstructions, and pipelines may move from charted locations or become uncovered due to the force of storm surges.  Storm surges and winds may also create shoals.  The U.S. Aids to Navigation System marking wrecks and obstructions is intended for use with nautical charts.  The exact meaning of a particular aid to navigation may not be clear to the mariner without referencing a nautical chart.  Mariners should exercise caution and report aid to navigation discrepancies and hazards to navigation to the nearest U.S. Coast Guard unit.

• LOCKS/BRIDGES/NAVIGATION STRUCTURES: Drawbridges, locks, and navigation structures along the coast may deviate from normal operating procedures in preparation for heavy weather events.  Some structures may be unable to open because of high winds, high water levels, or to facilitate evacuation of land traffic.  Mariners will be given as much notice as possible when structures are to be closed; however, these structures may close on short notice and well in advance of the storm.  Mariners should anticipate these closures and are urged to seek safe harbor as soon as possible.

• PORTS/WATERWAYS: As tropical weather approaches the Gulf Coast, all potentially affected U.S. Coast Guard Captains of the Port (COTP) will issue a series of Port Conditions to promote the safety of life, the environment, and the viability of the Marine Transportation System.  Port Conditions are issued on a set timeline prior to the arrival of gale force winds associated with a tropical activity and identify the status of the port.  Timelines associated with each port condition are subject to local modifications based upon circumstances, but are most typically issued as follows:

- WHISKEY: 72 hours in advance, OPEN to all commercial traffic. 
- X-RAY: 48 hours in advance, OPEN to all commercial traffic.
- YANKEE: 24 hours in advance, RESTRICTED with vessel traffic control measures in effect.
- ZULU: 12 hours in advance, CLOSED to all vessel traffic, except for movements or activities specifically authorized by the COTP.

• Additional requirements or actions to address port-specific safety concerns will be issued by the COTP in conjunction with each Port Condition.  After the passing of a hurricane, local COTPs will issue updates regarding the port status via Broadcast Notice to Mariners and MSIBs.  Mariners are urged to monitor all U.S. Coast Guard and National Weather Service notices and radio traffic closely throughout the Hurricane Season. Throughout the Houston Ship Channel, Menhaden have been known to accumulate in sea strainers and cause loss or reduction in propulsion, reduced maneuverability, and loss of water pressure within the firefighting systems.  This is typically a seasonal event primarily occurring in the months of March thru October (although vessels have reported Menhaden impacts year-round).  Menhaden are typically found in coastal and inland tidal waters, and can form large surface schools, appearing in near-shore Gulf waters.  Schools of fish can be drawn into the vessel’s sea chest, clogging the sea strainers, reducing cooling, and causing high water/oil temperatures.  In extreme cases, intake of these fish have choked entire coolant systems resulting in engine auto slowdowns or automatic shutdowns.  Any system that takes suction from the sea could be at risk.  The Lone Star Harbor Safety Committee’s Causality Analysis Workgroup (CAWG) developed Recommended Best Practices and a “Vessel Questionnaire on Cooling Water Impacts by Menhaden Fish".  All deep draft vessels operators are encouraged to follow the Recommended Best Practices and are asked to complete and submit the questionnaire to info@theagcteam.com.  The CAWG will coordinate with Texas Parks and Wildlife to identify peak periods of projected activity in the Houston Ship Channel and will make this data available to the vessel via the vessel agent. Two official Coast Guard notices intersect your track. Neither should restrict your transit tomorrow, but the check was incomplete (see below).

I checked the track as a straight line from 37.00, -76.10 to 36.88, -76.33, about 13.2 nm, with a 1 nm corridor on each side. The source was the USCG NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information layers.

**1. Marine construction: dredging, Elizabeth River (MSI #53466, CG District 5)**
- **Location:** Lambert's Point Pier 6, Norfolk. The notice polygon sits right at your end point, around 36.88, -76.33.
- **Valid:** Oct 9, 2026 to Jan 4, 2027, so it takes effect tomorrow.
- **Timing:** The notice text says dredging starts "on or about October 21, 2026". Tomorrow you probably won't meet active dredging.
- **What it describes:** The dredge KOKO V works with towing tugs and scows. Loaded scows are towed from Pier 6 to an unloader barge at Shirley's Plantation (Weanack Island).
- **Radio:** Vessels monitor VHF channel 13.
- **For you:** Expect tug and scow traffic near the Elizabeth River end of your track.

**2. Marine event: Marine Event Permit process notice (CG District 5)**
- **Valid:** Jun 3 to Nov 30, 2026.
- **What it is:** It's an administrative announcement about a new online permit application process for regattas, fireworks and similar events. Its polygon covers a very large part of the region.
- **For you:** It isn't a restriction or hazard, and you can ignore it for transit.

**Matches by category:** No hazards to navigation, safety zones, naval activity, space operations, temporary aids-to-navigation changes, TESS advisories or MSIBs matched in the layers that were checked.

**Limits of this check**
- **Incomplete safety-zone layer:** NAVCEN lists the `safeZoneLine_1` file but doesn't publish it (HTTP 404). Safety zones drawn as lines weren't checked. Zero safety-zone matches therefore doesn't prove there are none. This is a real gap in an area with heavy naval and commercial traffic.
- **Not covered:** Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices, Light List and aids-to-navigation discrepancies, and notices without geometry. It also doesn't cover non-USCG sources such as NOAA, NGA NAVAREA warnings, weather and tides.
- **Timing:** I ran the check at the current time, not at a specific time tomorrow. Both notices would be in effect tomorrow either way. Notices issued between now and your departure won't be included.

Before you leave, check the current Broadcast Notices to Mariners and the Local Notice to Mariners for Sector Virginia. Also call the Coast Guard or listen to VHF for any safety zones in the Hampton Roads and Norfolk area. This is official-notice information, not navigational advice.

# README summary
## USCG Navigation Restriction Resolver

Checks a location, vessel route, or geographic bounding box against official U.S. Coast Guard Navigation Center (NAVCEN) Maritime Safety Information (MSI) GeoJSON layers and returns a single structured record of intersecting maritime notices. Outputs include intersecting safety zones, hazards to navigation, marine construction, marine events, naval activity, space-operation areas, temporary aids-to-navigation changes, TESS advisories and geospatial MSIBs, with each notice’s official text, validity windows, geometry and source provenance. Spatial processing uses a local azimuthal-equidistant projection centered on the query so nautical-mile buffers and corridors represent true distances; reported distances are geodesic on the WGS84 ellipsoid. Notices are time-classified at the query time (active, upcoming, or unknown validity) and expired records are accounted for separately. Results include per-dataset coverage metadata and status for each NAVCEN file checked, flags for unpublished or unavailable files, and a coverage note when dataset files were listed but not served. Route queries are ordered by position along the route; point and area queries are ordered by distance. Source is the NAVCEN GeoJSON layers (no third‑party data).

## Use cases

- Pre-voyage information gathering and route screening  
- Maritime operations workflows and harbor/port reconnaissance  
- Marine construction planning and project impact assessment  
- Space-operation awareness near coastlines and maritime areas  
- Autonomous agent research and automated maritime compliance checks

**12 active USCG notices fall within 2 nm of your route** (42.50,‑70.80 → 42.54,‑70.87; about 3.9 nm long). The check ran on 2026‑10‑08 against USCG NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information. The results are not complete, because one layer couldn't be checked (see the last section).

## Marine construction (3)
All three are for removal of daybeacons by AGM Marine Contractors, using dredge PRONCKAI, deck barge THING and tug SITKA. Work is 6am–8pm daily, about Sep 28 to Nov 15/16, 2026. The vessels monitor VHF‑FM 13 and 16 and work on channel 68.
- **Bowditch Ledge Daybeacon** (Salem Sound), at 42°32.4'N 070°48.7'W. It is 1.59 nm from the route.
- **Abbott Rock Daybeacon** (Salem Harbor), at 42°31.8'N 070°51.7'W. It is 0.23 nm from the route.
- **Lobster Rock Daybeacon** (Salem Harbor), at 42°32.3'N 070°52.9'W. It is 0.53 nm from the route.

## Hazard to navigation (1)
- **Bass River shoaling.** Severe shoaling has been reported between Bass River Channel Buoys 2 and 9, with a severe decrease in channel width. The notice runs to 2039. It is 0.89 nm from the route (Chart 13275).

## Marine events (8)
Regattas in Marblehead Harbor and Salem Sound, all on Chart 13275, except the Beverly reenactment on Chart 13276. Most polygons intersect the route directly.
- **Etchells New England Championships:** Oct 8–11, 11am–4pm, about 30 boats, in Salem Sound and Marblehead Harbor.
- **Nessa Keelboat High School Championships:** Oct 10, 9am–4pm, and Oct 11, 9am–12pm.
- **Beverly 400 Battle of the Hannah and Nautilus reenactment:** Oct 10, 9–11am, in Beverly Harbor off Independence Park, with 2 sailing vessels. It intersects the route's end.
- **Pumpkin Pursuit Race 2:** Oct 17 (the notice says Sunday), 12–4pm, about 15 boats.
- **Halloween Team Race:** Oct 24–25, 9am–4pm.
- **Pumpkin Pursuit Race 3:** Oct 24, 12–4pm.
- **Fall Laser ILCA Series:** Sundays, Sep 13 – Nov 22, 1–3pm, about 15 boats at 14'. The polygon intersects the route.
- **BYC MIT Tech Dinghy Frostbiting Series:** Sundays, Nov 8, 2026 – Apr 4, 2027, 12–2pm, in Marblehead Harbor. It is 0.35 nm from the route. The notice's record window starts Oct 8, but the text gives Nov 8 as the first race.

## What wasn't checked
- **Safety zones:** the USCG file for this layer (`safeZoneLine_1`) returned a 404, so safety zones were not checked. Zero safety‑zone results here does not mean none exist.
- **Other gaps:** Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices, aids‑to‑navigation discrepancies, and non‑USCG sources (NOAA, NGA NAVAREA warnings) were not covered.
- **Not for navigation:** this is information only. Check current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners and VHF broadcasts before transiting.

The zone is enforced from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily, and only while construction work is under way. You may not enter, remain in or transit through it during enforcement unless the Captain of the Port New York authorizes it. Some full-channel closures are scheduled, including 22–26 June 2026, but the text says these dates may change.
- **Larchmont fireworks zone:** The database still marks it "active" because its record window runs to December 2026. The notice text says it was only enforced on July 3, 2026, from 9:00 to 10:30 p.m., and that date has passed.

This rule is effective without notice from December 3, 2024, through 5 p.m. on May 27, 2027. This area is intended for the vessels and machinery being used by personnel for the Glen Island Bridge rehabilitation project. finalAnswer:
No active USCG safety zone covers 41.35, -72.10 itself. One active zone is nearby, and the check was incomplete (details below).

**New London Harbor – Shaw Cove Entrance** (NAVCEN record MSI UID 53516)
- **Distance:** Its center is at about 41°21′01″N, 72°05′42″W (41.3503, -72.0950). That is roughly 0.23 nm from your point, so your point is inside the 5 nm search area but not inside the zone.
- **Type:** Temporary safety zone, Coast Guard District 1.
- **Area:** All navigable waters of the Thames River within a 600-foot radius of that position, near New London Waterfront Park, New London, CT.
- **Event:** A drone show. The zone was in force on September 12, 2026, from 8:15 to 9:30 p.m. The notice itself is listed as valid from 2026-09-11 to 2027-03-13.
- **Rule:** No vessel or person may enter without permission from the Captain of the Port (COTP) or a designated representative.
- **Contact:** The person in charge of the drone show is Jeff Ward, (516) 369-2107.

The 600-foot radius is about 0.1 nm, which is smaller than the 0.23 nm gap. So even while the zone is in force, it should not reach your exact coordinate. That is my own estimate. It is not a value the actor reported.

**The check was incomplete.** NAVCEN lists a dataset of line-type safety zones (`safeZoneLine_1`) but returns a 404 for it, so those records weren't checked. Zero matches for line-type zones therefore doesn't mean none exist. I also only searched safety zones, not other notice types such as hazards or marine events. The search doesn't cover Broadcast Notices to Mariners.

This is not navigational advice. Before transiting, check the current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners, VHF broadcasts, and the Sector Long Island Sound COTP.

  - Work is at about 36°58'16"N 76°24'57"W, weekdays 0700–1530.
  - Vessels should keep to no wake within 500 ft and monitor VHF 13 and 16.
- MSI 53462, Kinder Morgan Bulk Terminals dredging, Newport News: 4.8 nm away, active 24 Sep 2026 to 4 Jan 2027.

I found 4 current USCG Local Notice to Mariners records within 3 nm of 21.46, -157.76 (Kaneohe Bay and Mokapu Peninsula, Oahu). All four are active as of 2026-10-08. The search is not complete, because one layer couldn't be checked (details below).

| # | MSI UID | Category | Location | Distance | Effective window |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3943 | Naval activity (gunnery exercises) | Kaneohe Bay, Sampan Channel | 0 nm (point is inside the polygon) | 2024-10-30 to 2028-06-28 |
| 2 | 23349 | Hazard to navigation | Mokapu Peninsula | 0.54 nm | 2025-07-10 to 2027-01-01 |
| 3 | 3937 | Naval activity (military operations) | Kaneohe Bay | 1.46 nm | 2024-10-30 to 2028-07-31 |
| 4 | 3944 | Naval activity (gunnery exercises) | Sector Honolulu Territorial Sea / EEZ | 1.61 nm | 2024-10-30 to 2028-07-31 |

**Details**
1. **3943, Pyramid Rock / Fort Hase / Kaneohe Bay Danger Zone**
   - The zone is closed at all times to surface craft, swimmers and divers, except authorized personnel.
   - The only listed operation for Oct 5–16 is a Wed Oct 14 helicopter SAR exercise at the Pyramid Rock lighthouse, 0900–1400.
2. **23349, Wave Energy Converter (OE-35) failure**
   - The converter's port sea duct failed structurally, and four large pieces (up to 22 MT) fell to the seafloor.
   - Further failure is possible. Mariners are asked to stay 1000 ft from the buoy.
3. **3937, military amphibious and search-and-rescue operations**
   - These may happen at any time, day or night, about 0.5 nm south of Mokapu Peninsula.
   - Contact Waterfront Operations on VHF Ch 82A or at (808) 257-2941, especially if you use sonar, to avoid endangering divers.
4. **3944, Ulupau Crater danger zone**
   - Vessels must leave the zone at best speed by the most direct route.
   - Hazardous operations are listed for Zones 1 and 2 on most days of Oct 5–16, mainly 0000–0200 and 0600–2359. There are none on Oct 10–12, and Oct 13 is 0600–2359 only.

**Coverage gap:** The Coast Guard's `safeZoneLine_1` safety-zone file is listed in its index but returns a 404 (not published). Safety-zone records in that file were not checked, so there could be safety zones near this point that aren't shown here. No expired records were excluded.

**Scope:** The data comes from the Coast Guard's NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information layers. Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices, Light List data and aids-to-navigation discrepancies aren't covered. This is informational, not navigational advice, so check current official Notices to Mariners and VHF broadcasts before relying on it.

# README summary
## USCG Navigation Restriction Resolver

Checks a location, vessel route, or geographic bounding box against official U.S. Coast Guard Navigation Center (NAVCEN) Maritime Safety Information (MSI) GeoJSON layers and returns a single structured record of intersecting maritime notices. Outputs include intersecting safety zones, hazards to navigation, marine construction, marine events, naval activity, space-operation areas, temporary aids-to-navigation changes, TESS advisories and geospatial MSIBs, with each notice’s official text, validity windows, geometry and source provenance. Spatial processing uses a local azimuthal-equidistant projection centered on the query so nautical-mile buffers and corridors represent true distances; reported distances are geodesic on the WGS84 ellipsoid. Notices are time-classified at the query time (active, upcoming, or unknown validity) and expired records are accounted for separately. Results include per-dataset coverage metadata and status for each NAVCEN file checked, flags for unpublished or unavailable files, and a coverage note when dataset files were listed but not served. Route queries are ordered by position along the route; point and area queries are ordered by distance. Source is the NAVCEN GeoJSON layers (no third‑party data).

## Use cases

- Pre-voyage information gathering and route screening  
- Maritime operations workflows and harbor/port reconnaissance  
- Marine construction planning and project impact assessment  
- Space-operation awareness near coastlines and maritime areas  
- Autonomous agent research and automated maritime compliance checks

Yes. The USCG Navigation Center's Maritime Safety Information shows two active space-operation hazard areas within 25 nm of 33.80°N, 119.30°W. I checked as of 2026-10-08 21:07 UTC. Neither area contains your point.

**1. NASA Crew-12 reentry and splashdown, Los Angeles site (Sector Los Angeles, Territorial Sea)**
- **Distance:** about 2.3 nm from your point. This is the closest area, and its boundary nearly touches your position.
- **Effective window:** 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-20 (UTC). The notice text gives the hazardous operations as 05 Oct 16:35 UTC to 19 Oct 19:05 UTC.
- **Type:** Hazardous Warning Area, Significant National Interest.
- **Boundary:** 33.78N 119.25W → 33.75N 119.30W → 33.60N 119.30W → 33.55N 119.233W → 33.55N 119.117W → 33.617N 119.033W → 33.75N 119.033W → 33.783N 119.083W.
- **Contact:** SpaceX, regulatory@spacex.com, or VHF-FM channel 05, 06 or 16.

**2. SpaceX Starlink g15-25 launch (Sector San Diego, EEZ)**
- **Distance:** about 24.7 nm. It only just falls inside your 25 nm radius.
- **Effective window:** 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-18 (UTC).
- **Type:** Hazardous Warning Area, Commercial.
- **Shape:** a long strip running from near Point Conception, around 34.6N 120.6W, southeast to about 28.2N 117.3W.
- **Primary window:** 10 Oct 23:00Z to 11 Oct 03:25Z (Hazard Area A) or 03:43Z (Hazard Area B). Backup days run daily at the same times through 16–17 Oct.

Mariners are advised to stay clear of both areas while operations are underway.

This covers only USCG NAVCEN Local Notice to Mariners geospatial records. It does not cover Broadcast Notices to Mariners, NGA NAVAREA warnings, or records without geometry. It's also not navigational advice, so check current Notices to Mariners and VHF broadcasts before transiting.

For each chokepoint it reports latest daily transits and tanker transits, short-term (7‑day) and medium-term (30‑day) averages with year‑over‑year comparisons, a disruption level determined by percent change versus the same window one year earlier (severity tiers), 7‑day breakdowns by ship type (tanker, container, dry bulk, general cargo, ro‑ro) and average carried capacity in tons, plus optional daily history (up to 400 days). It also emits one record per active navigational warning containing NAVAREA/subregion identifiers, message metadata, full warning text, region tags (Persian Gulf/Hormuz, Red Sea/Gulf of Aden, Black Sea/Ukraine, Eastern Mediterranean, Taiwan/South China Sea, Baltic) and risk keywords (missile, firing, drone, GNSS jamming, mine, piracy, etc.). I found two active marine construction notices in the East River between 40.70,-73.98 and 40.76,-73.95. Both come from USCG NAVCEN Local Notice to Mariners data, checked on 2026-10-08.

**1. East River Main Channel, Montgomery St to E 14th St (MSI #913)**
- **Dates:** 2022-01-03 to 2026-12-30.
- **Work:** The notice covers esplanade, bulkhead and park reconstruction. The listed contractor is IPCP.
- **Hours:** 5–7 days a week, 6:00am–6:00pm.
- **Area:** A long, narrow strip along the Manhattan shoreline, from about 40.709°N, -73.984°W up to 40.727°N, -73.971°W.
- **Equipment:** Tugboat DEBRA QUINN, an inspection boat, mooring barges, a gantry crane barge, a crawler crane barge, deck barges and hopper barges.
- **Vessel moves:** Tugboats move the vessels at any time of day or night.
- **VHF:** Monitoring channels 13 and 66.
- **Guidance:** Transit at your slowest safe speed to minimize wake, and arrange passing before you go by.

**2. East River Main Channel, Water Club and E 34th St Heliport (MSI #26111)**
- **Dates:** 2025-09-01 to 2027-07-05. The notice text says work runs from September 15, 2025.
- **Work:** Diver operations at the marginal wharf platforms. The listed contractor is Phoenix Marine Co.
- **Hours:** 6:00am–2:00pm.
- **Area:** A small polygon between about 40.7399°N and 40.7427°N, near -73.972°W.
- **Equipment:** One crane barge, one material barge and one work platform barge.
- **VHF:** Monitoring channel 9.
- **Guidance:** Use extreme caution and transit at the slowest safe speed to minimize wake.

**Coverage limits:**
- The data doesn't include Broadcast Notices to Mariners.
- It also leaves out bridge work, notices without geometry, and non-USCG sources such as NOAA and NGA.
- Before transiting, check the current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners, and listen on VHF. This is not navigational advice.

finalAnswer:
Yes. A search of the Coast Guard's NAVCEN Maritime Safety Information datasets found two active marine construction notices within 5 nautical miles of 38.89, -77.05. I checked all four marine construction layers, and none had errors.

**1. Tidal Basin and West Potomac Park Seawall Rehabilitation** (MSI UID 270)
- **Distance:** About 0.16 nm from your point. The notice area is a polygon along the West Potomac Park shoreline, and the point itself falls just outside it.
- **Dates:** Active from 2024-09-09 to 2027-02-01. Waterside work is expected to finish by the end of 2026.
- **Work:** Cianbro Corporation is doing the work for the National Park Service. The notice lists:
  - Two temporary trestles, about 94 ft into the river and about 55 ft into the Tidal Basin.
  - Turbidity curtains and two monitoring buoys.
  - Crane barges, material barges and other boats.
- **Work area:** It runs along the shoreline from Arlington Memorial Bridge to the Inlet Bridge.
- **Mariner request:** Stay out of the work area and keep wake to a minimum.
- **Waterway and district:** Listed under the Chesapeake Channel / Potomac River, Coast Guard District 5.

**2. Long Bridge and Pedestrian Bridge construction moorings** (MSI UID 31521)
- **Distance:** About 0.97 nm from your point, at 38°52'55.9"N, 77°01'54.9"W in the Georgetown Channel, Coast Guard District 5.
- **Dates:** Active from 2025-11-04 to 2030-01-01.
- **Work:** North Skanska Flatiron Joint Venture is installing mooring anchors and buoys. It is driving 36" steel piles and building a trestle across the Washington Channel to widen the CSX Long Bridge. The trestle will stop about 200 ft from the existing bridge.
- **Mooring location:** The anchors will sit about 130 ft from the southeast shore, between the CSX Long Bridge and the I-395 Bridge.

**Limits**
- The search did not cover Broadcast Notices to Mariners, bridge notices, records without geometry, or non-Coast Guard sources such as NOAA or NGA.
- This is not navigational advice. Before transiting, check current Local and Broadcast Notices to Mariners, VHF broadcasts and official charts.

The data comes from the Actor `rhincodontypus/uscg-navigation-restriction-resolver`. Its source is https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/msi.
